data.title: bn-2ij: M1.1.3 Runs and request keys persisted before any effect
data.description:
Implements bn-2ij acceptance as local coordination metadata at HEAD 2403c3216cab32f0a8037f533ce7b6906fd26e32 (parent 5009a9b).

- crates/scourge-core/src/request.rs: normalization to scourge.request-input.v1 (canonical command path and aliases, declared CLI defaults 2 rounds / sequential, typed argument shape, member order irrelevant, array order and string contents preserved, presentation flags / bound path / actor / key excluded).
- crates/scourge-core/src/store/003_request_keys.sql: request_keys table binding key -> engagement, resolved binding, command, canonical input bytes + digest, run, receipt revision and first-acceptance selector snapshot.
- crates/scourge-core/src/store/mod.rs: declare_request (normalized input + run + steps + snapshot in one Immediate transaction, audit request.accept, before any effect boundary), reopen_request (byte equality before re-resolving anything, returns original receipt and current run state, writes nothing), find_request (unknown and foreign keys both absent), typed StoreError::error_code for OBJECT_NOT_FOUND/3, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED/4, REVISION_CONFLICT/4, CONFLICTING_RUN/4, INTEGRITY_FAILURE/6; lead revisions are a compare-and-set.
- Tests: first-boundary crash with a local counter sentinel only, lost-response reopen before and after finalization, same and different input, wrong-scope indistinguishability, lead revision conflicts, failed/idempotent writes advance neither revision nor audit, and 9 normalization equality/inequality tests.

Validation: cargo test -p scourge-core (23 lib, 15 contract, 9 request_input, 2 doc) and just check exit 0 with TMPDIR=/home/bob/src/scourge/.maw/cache/t. No network, target, credential, replay or external effect is performed anywhere in this change.

data.body:
severity:medium — declare_request adopts and rewrites an existing runs row, erasing a finalized outcome.

`declare_request` gates only on `request_keys` (mod.rs:327) and then calls `insert_run` (mod.rs:334). Its `put_run` upsert (mod.rs:495-512) overwrites `state, flags, effects, oracle_result, reproduction, cleanup` whenever `(engagement_id, request_key, experiment_digest)` match. Nothing checks that `run.id` has no prior `run.record`/`request.accept` audit event or that the stored run is still `declared`, so this acceptance path bypasses the receipt CAS that `record_run` relies on (see `stale_writer_cannot_overwrite_run_outcomes_or_clear_a_finalized_run` in store/tests.rs).

Reproduction (standalone harness against this exact HEAD, local SQLite only, no product edits):
1. `record_run(run, None)`, then `record_run(finalized { state=finalized, oracle_result=true, effects=observed, cleanup=complete }, Some(receipt))`.
2. `declare_request(scope, input, same run as declared)` returns `Ok` with a new receipt.
3. `reopen_request` then reports `state=declared`, `oracle_result=None`, `effects=none`, `cleanup=not_required`. The finalized result and observed effects are gone, and the audit log shows a normal `request.accept`.

Reachable on a real upgrade path: migration 003 does not backfill `request_keys`, so every run recorded under schema v2 (including a finalized run with unresolved `effects=unknown`) has `runs.request_key` without a `request_keys` row. A retry of that key that ends in `declare_request` with the stored run adopts and resets it. Reproduced from a hand-built `user_version=2` store: legacy finalized `R-legacy` was adopted and reset to `declared`, new receipt 2.

Why it matters: it hides unresolved effects (INV-14) and rewrites durable run evidence through the path this bone adds. Fix: refuse an existing `runs` row in the declare path (strict INSERT, or require `state=declared` and no prior audit for that run id), and add a v2-to-v3 legacy-run case to request_tests.rs.

severity:low — the stored request row is not integrity-checked on read: the key-to-run binding and canonical bytes can be altered without INTEGRITY_FAILURE.

`matches` (mod.rs:125-130) compares only the caller canonical bytes against the stored columns. `acceptance`/`load_run` (mod.rs:568,585) load the run by `request_keys.run_id` but never check `runs.request_key == key`, and migration 003 has no `UNIQUE(run_id)` or cross-table constraint tying the columns together (003_request_keys.sql:4-18). The only tie is the FK to `runs(engagement_id, id)`.

Reproductions (same-account raw SQLite writes, then `reopen_request`; local harness):
1. `UPDATE request_keys SET run_id=<another run of the same engagement>` -> reopen returns that other run under the same key and the original receipt, no error. The key-to-run association is not verified.
2. Reorder the stored `input` object members so the bytes are semantically identical but non-canonical (digest untouched) -> replay fails as `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` instead of `INTEGRITY_FAILURE`, and a non-canonical stored value permanently denies every replay of that key.
3. Replace `input_digest` with an unrelated digest -> same reuse error even though the stored bytes match.
4. Rewrite `input` and `input_digest` to another canonical object -> reopen accepts the forged input as equal.

Severity is low because it needs write access to the coordination database, but the ADR states altered or missing canonical bytes are `INTEGRITY_FAILURE`. Suggested hardening: verify the stored bytes with `canonical::from_canonical_slice` plus digest, assert `load_run(...).request_key == key` and engagement equality, and add `UNIQUE(run_id)` to `request_keys`.

severity:low — caller-supplied selectors are snapshotted without validation, and a lead ID from another engagement resolves into this engagement receipt (INV-25 / plan §8.6).

`resolve_selectors` (mod.rs:655-690) takes an explicit `engagement_revision`/`lead_revision` with `as_u64()` and stores it without checking that the revision exists. It resolves `lead_id`/`finding_id` with `SELECT MAX(revision) FROM lead_revisions WHERE lead_id=?` (mod.rs:679) with no `engagement_id` predicate.

Reproductions (local harness, exact HEAD):
- `declare_request(scope("local"), verify { lead_id: "L-1", engagement_revision: 987654 }, run)` returns `Ok` with `acceptance.engagement_revision == 987654`, although no such revision exists. The receipt attests a nonexistent selector.
- Engagement `second` holds lead L with revisions 1 through 4. `declare_request(scope("local"), verify { lead_id: L }, run)` returns `Ok` with `acceptance.lead_revision == Some(4)`, and the run is created under `local`. The response reveals another engagement lead revision for an ID lookup, while the contract says an ID lookup never reveals another engagement.

Severity is low because LeadIds are 128-bit random identities and later verification linkage is FK-checked, but the acceptance should reject a foreign lead (`OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, indistinguishable from absent) and an explicit revision that does not exist, or resolve with `AND engagement_id = ?` and validate the revision.

severity:low — concurrency semantics: an identical concurrent acceptance answers OBJECT_NOT_FOUND, and lock contention surfaces as INTEGRITY_FAILURE.

(a) Same-input concurrent acceptance. `declare_request` returns `StoreError::RequestNotFound` for any existing key, same input included (mod.rs:327-329); only `reopen_request` returns the original acceptance. Two separate connections declaring the same key and input concurrently produce exactly one `Ok` plus one `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` in 120/120 iterations, with one run row and one key row (so no second start, as required). A surface that implements reopen-then-declare has a TOCTOU window: if the first writer commits between the two calls, the retry reports `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` for a key whose acceptance is already durable. The ADR requires same-input reuse to return the original run; consider one atomic accept-or-reopen entry point, or have `declare_request` return the stored acceptance when `matches` holds.

(b) Lock contention. `Store::open` sets journal/foreign_keys/synchronous but no busy policy, and `reopen_request` uses an `Immediate` write transaction (mod.rs:378-379) even though a replay writes nothing. With a held write lock, a declaration blocked for 5.004 s (rusqlite default busy timeout) then returned `StoreError::Database(DatabaseBusy)` -> `INTEGRITY_FAILURE` / 6. A read-only replay can hit the same path. Exit 6 reads as corruption, not as a retryable conflict/dependency; consider a short busy timeout and a typed busy/conflict code, and a deferred transaction for reopen/find.

Related, structural (not reproduced): `find_request` (mod.rs:391+) runs its key lookup and run load as two statements outside any transaction, so a concurrent writer can make the returned run state inconsistent with the stored receipt.

severity:info — verified behaviour, test record and non-blocking nits (informational; can be resolved with the review).

Verified at HEAD 2403c3216cab32f0a8037f533ce7b6906fd26e32 (base 5009a9b6ec79e881a3c34d59ad7454019eeb8485), workspace clean apart from the untracked Seal review directory:
- Normalization (`request.rs`): bare invocation plus `tldr`/`brief`/`onboard` collapse to `status`; internal whitespace collapses; declared defaults (`rounds=2`, `mode=sequential`) equal explicit values; member order is irrelevant at depth; array order, case and string contents are preserved; typed shapes reject unknown members, wrong types, `rounds=null`, and untyped shapes; `format`, workspace path, actor and the key are absent from the stored bytes. Frozen `fixtures/contracts/scourge-v1/request-input.json` equals the normalized `verify` request. 36 distinct typed inputs produced 36 distinct canonical byte strings and read back byte-identically.
- Acceptance/replay: `declare_request` commits exactly one `request.accept` audit event, `receipt_revision == audit revision == store revision`, `request_keys.input` is exactly the canonical bytes and digest, and `runs.request_key == request_keys.key`. A replay from a new connection returns the identical acceptance and leaves a full-table dump unchanged (no revision, audit, run or key write). After finalization, a replay returns the original receipt with the current finalized state. `record_run(None)` after an acceptance is a typed `CONFLICTING_RUN`; `record_run(Some(receipt))` works even after an individually recorded step; a stale receipt is refused.
- Lost acknowledgement and first-boundary crash: a child process declared a run (with a bundled step), then aborted. From a new connection, `reopen_request` returned the same run, receipt and step, with exactly one run row and one key row. No external effect exists in the product change.
- Scope: an unknown key, a foreign engagement and a foreign binding produce the same `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` (Display, Debug and code) and write nothing; a foreign run object gets `CONFLICTING_RUN` before any key lookup, so key ownership is not distinguishable.
- Selector snapshot: frozen at first acceptance across a later lead edit and manifest append; a null selector resolves once and is never re-resolved on replay.
- Typed errors: reuse = `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`/4, revision = `REVISION_CONFLICT`/4, conflicting run = 4, absent = `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`/3, database/overflow = `INTEGRITY_FAILURE`/6. A store-revision overflow and a selector above the SQLite integer range both rolled back with no run, key or audit row.
- Migrations/constraints: v2 to v3 sets `user_version=3`, appends one `schema.migrate` event and retains runs; a foreign `application_id` and a populated version-0 file are refused; STRICT tables, FK pragma, WAL and `synchronous=FULL` hold. 003 adds the key/engagement/binding/command/input/digest/run/receipt/selector columns with the documented checks.
- No network, target, credential, replay or external effect is added: the change contains no process, socket or HTTP code; tests use local SQLite, local counters and a simulated abort only.

Test commands run (offline): `cargo test --workspace --locked` = 23 lib + 15 contract + 9 request_input + 9 store + 2 doc plus the fixture suites, all green; a 25-test adversarial harness at `.maw/cache/review-bn2ij/harness/tests/review.rs` (scratch, outside the workspace, not committed) reproduces every finding and the checks above.

Non-blocking nits:
1. A caller-supplied `Run` with two identical step numbers collapses to one stored step on reopen (declare keeps only the last); no error is returned.
2. `request_key_scopes` (003:20) is not used by any statement in this commit.
3. `NormalizedInput::read` accepts non-canonical bytes. The store never uses it, but a future surface must not treat it as canonical input.
4. `record_run` still allows a finalized run to move back to `declared` when given the latest receipt (pre-existing M1.1.2 behaviour, outside this diff, but it interacts with finding th-3pzown).
5. Unregistered command arguments stay untyped and unvalidated; the frozen exclusion applies to registered shapes and to `Surface`, which is satisfied.

data.reason:
BLOCK on 2403c3216cab32f0a8037f533ce7b6906fd26e32 (base 5009a9b). Normalization, receipt, scope indistinguishability, selector snapshots, replay-no-write, lost-ack recovery, typed errors, constraints and migration all verify green, but four reproduction-backed threads remain open:

1. th-3pzown (medium): declare_request adopts an existing runs row and resets a finalized/observed run to declared, erasing oracle_result, effects and cleanup, including every pre-003 run after the v2-to-v3 migration. This bypasses the record_run receipt CAS and can hide unresolved effects (INV-14).
2. th-3qhl0u (low): stored request rows have no read-time integrity gate: altering run_id returns a different run under the key, and reordered/edited canonical bytes or digest return IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED instead of INTEGRITY_FAILURE.
3. th-1chb3n (low): explicit engagement_revision/lead_revision are snapshotted without validation, and a lead_id owned by another engagement resolves its revision into this engagement receipt (INV-25 ID-lookup scope).
4. th-zvjwo8 (low): concurrent identical acceptance answers OBJECT_NOT_FOUND (reopen-then-declare has a TOCTOU window), and a held write lock becomes INTEGRITY_FAILURE after 5 s; reopen takes an Immediate write transaction for a read-only replay.

th-1b6xlj is an informational record of verified behaviour, tests and nits. No product source was edited by this review; workspace HEAD and claims are untouched. Tests: cargo test --workspace --locked offline green (23 lib, 15 contracts, 9 request_input, 9 store, 2 doc, plus fixture suites) and a 25-test adversarial harness at .maw/cache/review-bn2ij/harness/tests/review.rs.

data.body: Fixed in c2b32c2. declare_request no longer reaches the run upsert: the mint path calls create_run, which refuses any run ID already in runs (in-transaction existence check, then a strict INSERT) and rolls the whole acceptance back with CONFLICTING_RUN/4. Nothing reads or rewrites state, flags, effects, oracle_result, reproduction or cleanup, so a finalized or unresolved-effect run cannot be adopted; record_run keeps its receipt CAS unchanged and remains the only path that settles an outcome. A migrated v2 run has no key row, so reopen is OBJECT_NOT_FOUND and declare is CONFLICTING_RUN with the run row unchanged. Regressions: store::request_tests::a_declaration_never_adopts_or_rewrites_an_existing_run_row (finalized with effects=unknown and cleanup=failed, plus a declared-only row) and a_migrated_legacy_run_is_never_adopted_by_a_declaration (hand-built user_version=2 store with a finalized unknown-effects row and a declared row; migration to schema 4; both declarations refused; zero key rows).

Fixed in c2b32c2. Read-time gate: StoredRequest::verify recomputes SHA-256 over the stored bytes, requires them canonical and shape-valid via NormalizedInput::read_canonical, requires the command column to agree with those bytes, and requires the selector snapshot to be paired. acceptance() then binds key->run->engagement both ways (runs.request_key == key, engagement equal) and requires receipt_revision to name the request.accept audit event for that run. Every failure is StoreError::Integrity -> INTEGRITY_FAILURE/6 on reopen_request, find_request and declare_request; never reuse, a different run or not-found. Migration 004_request_key_integrity.sql adds UNIQUE(request_key_runs) on run_id so one run maps to one key. Regressions: a_tampered_stored_request_row_is_an_integrity_failure covers seven raw-SQL cases (non-canonical member order, digest, key->run, run->key, command column, receipt, selector pairing) through all three paths and asserts no row or revision is written; one_run_holds_at_most_one_request_key. Remaining limit stated plainly: a wholly consistent rewrite of input+digest+command by a same-account writer is indistinguishable without an external anchor; every internal inconsistency now fails integrity, which matches the ADR chain model.

Fixed in c2b32c2. resolve_selectors validates selectors: an explicit engagement_revision must exist in engagement_revisions for the selected engagement, a lead or finding selector must join leads.engagement_id = the selected engagement, and an explicit lead_revision must exist for that lead in that engagement. Failures are StoreError::SelectorNotFound -> OBJECT_NOT_FOUND/3 with one fixed message, so a foreign and an absent lead/revision are indistinguishable and no revision is echoed; the declaration rolls back completely. Replays still compare stored bytes and never re-resolve, so existing acceptances stay replayable. Intended consequence: naming a lead absent from the engagement now refuses acceptance instead of snapshotting a null revision. Tests: explicit_revisions_must_exist_in_the_selected_engagement (absent engagement_revision 987654, absent lead_revision 3, then existing 1/1 accepted) and a_foreign_selector_is_indistinguishable_from_an_absent_one (verify lead_id and retest finding_id pointing at another engagement lead with four revisions; identical Display, code and exit, nothing written; the same lead resolves inside its own engagement).

Fixed in c2b32c2. (a) declare_request is atomic accept-or-reopen: it replays from a deferred read snapshot first, and the Immediate mint path re-reads the key after taking the write lock and returns the stored acceptance when the input matches (IdempotencyKeyReused otherwise). A reopen-then-declare surface therefore has no TOCTOU window, and concurrent identical callers both get the one original acceptance with no extra row, revision or audit. (b) Store::open sets a 500 ms busy timeout and SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED map to StoreError::Busy -> CONFLICTING_RUN/4 (retryable), not INTEGRITY_FAILURE; reopen_request and find_request use deferred read transactions and a replay never takes a write lock. find_request reads the key row and its run in one snapshot. Tests: concurrent_identical_acceptance_is_one_original_receipt (30 iterations, separate connections, both Ok, identical acceptance, revision == receipt, one run/one key/one accept audit), concurrent_mismatched_acceptance_is_reuse_not_absence (20 iterations: one Ok plus one IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, never OBJECT_NOT_FOUND), a_held_write_lock_is_a_typed_conflict_and_replays_stay_readable (BEGIN IMMEDIATE held: reopen/find answer, mint fails Busy/CONFLICTING_RUN/4 inside the short timeout and succeeds after release), a_lookup_never_mixes_a_key_row_with_another_snapshot. Independent harness: 200 x 3-caller identical races and 200 replay-vs-mint races, green.

Addressed in c2b32c2. (1) Duplicate step numbers are refused: validate_steps rejects a repeated number in the strict creation path and in record_run with CONFLICTING_RUN/4 and nothing written, instead of last-wins; regression a_run_names_each_step_once. (2) request_key_scopes is gone: 003 no longer creates it and migration 004 drops it with DROP INDEX IF EXISTS; the only request_keys index is UNIQUE(request_key_runs) on run_id. (3) NormalizedInput::read is documented as lenient and explicitly non-authoritative, and the new NormalizedInput::read_canonical enforces canonical bytes plus the registered argument shape; every authoritative store read uses it (tests/request_input.rs covers canonical accept, reordered/whitespace reject, wrong-shape reject). (4) record_run's finalized->declared transition with the latest receipt is pre-existing M1.1.2 behavior outside this diff, left unchanged as this bone requires, and it is no longer reachable through the acceptance path now that declare cannot adopt a run. (5) Unregistered command arguments stay untyped under the frozen exclusion, with Surface excluded as recorded.

data.reason: Verified at integrated HEAD 47cac208323d8392e51df425dca54ac7df668ea9: declare_request uses strict create_run and refuses every existing run ID before selector/audit/key writes. Finalized unknown-effect/failed-cleanup state and hand-built v2 migrated rows remain byte-for-byte durable; both regression tests pass and no key/audit/revision is minted.

Verified at integrated HEAD 47cac208323d8392e51df425dca54ac7df668ea9: StoredRequest::verify recomputes digest, requires canonical typed input and command/snapshot agreement; acceptance binds key to run, run to key and engagement, and receipt to request.accept. Seven tamper cases exercise reopen/find/declare as INTEGRITY_FAILURE with no writes, and schema 004 enforces one key per run.

Verified at integrated HEAD 47cac208323d8392e51df425dca54ac7df668ea9: explicit engagement and lead revisions must exist, lead/finding lookup joins through the selected engagement, and absent versus foreign selectors share OBJECT_NOT_FOUND without revision or identity disclosure. Focused existence and cross-engagement regressions pass.

Verified at integrated HEAD 47cac208323d8392e51df425dca54ac7df668ea9: declare_request performs deferred replay then rechecks under the Immediate mint transaction; identical races return one receipt, mismatched races return IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, reads use one deferred snapshot, and SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED maps after the 500 ms timeout to retryable CONFLICTING_RUN. All concurrency regressions pass.

Informational record verified and addressed at integrated HEAD 47cac208323d8392e51df425dca54ac7df668ea9: duplicate step numbers are refused, the unused scope index is removed, authoritative reads require canonical typed input, and the acceptance path cannot reach the pre-existing record_run state transition. Full core and workspace gates pass; no external effect code is present.

LGTM at exact integrated target 47cac208323d8392e51df425dca54ac7df668ea9 over current base a3040ca1917b6934ced7b36520e899f9c1784661. The initial independent security review found four concrete failures; the fixed stack now closes each structurally and with non-vacuous regressions. Lead rerun: 72 core unit, 15 contract, 10 engagement/policy, 10 request-input, 2 doc tests, plus full just check all green. Lost-ack replay remains write-free; failures are typed; no target, credential, network, process, or external-effect code is added.
